subject: Not writing truncated beta prior distribution correctly?

messages.author: 4e9f2d72eb0a8b62
messages.subject: Not writing truncated beta prior distribution correctly?
parts:
Hi all,

I need help with truncated beta prior distribution for a model parameter. Attached is stan code and Rscript that runs well.

Errors occur when I replaced beta prior distribution for theta (in model block), which is 

theta ~ beta(0.5, 0.5), with a truncated beta prior distribution end at 0.2, as following:

for (i in 1:G)
for (j in 1:N)
theta[i*j] ~ beta(0.5, 0.5) T[0.0, 0.2]

I got some errors about failure to validate transformed parameters, that p exceeded 1 while it should be restrained to [0, 1].

I therefore inserted inv_logit to p (as follows) and replaced binomial_logit to binomial

for (i in 1:G)
for (j in 1:N)
p[i, j] <- inv_logit(theta0[i] + weighted_theta[i] * x1[j]) 

However the following error remains which I'm not sure how to debug.

[377] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                                             
[378] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                                         
[379] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                                       
[380] "Exception thrown at line 62: []: accessing element out of range. index 6 out of range; expecting index to be between 1 and 5; index position = 1theta"
[381] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"               
[382] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."   

Any comments will be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

Huiying

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Not writing truncated beta prior distribution correctly?
parts:
The parameter theta needs to be declared with <lower=0, upper = 0.2>.
In general, every legal value of a parameter according to the constraints
must have support (finite log density) in the model.

- Bob
